3 03-11-2025 Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the State.

2. The petitioner is apprehending his arrest in connection with Complaint Case No. 769(c) of 2022 registered for the offences punishable under Sections 323, 504, 341, 506 and 498(A) of the Indian Penal Code and Section  of the D.P. Act.
3. As per the prosecution case, the petitioner and the co-accused persons are alleged to have tortured the informant mentally and physically due to non-fulfillment of demand of dowry.

sentences.text: There is general and omnibus allegation against the petitioner who is the husband of the complainant.
The petitioner neither demanded any dowry nor tortured the informant/complainant.

The petitioner has relied upon the judgment of this Court in the case of "Md. Naimul Haque Ansari @ Naimul Haque Ansari & Ors. Vs. The State of Bihar, reported in 2006(3) PLJR 182."
Learned counsel has further submitted that Section 498A of the IPC is triable by the Magistrate.

sentences.text: The petitioner has one criminal antecedent in which he is on bail as stated in para 3 of the bail petition.

The dispute between both the parties has been resolved amicably on 09.10.2025 through the process of the Mediation Proceeding on the following terms and conditions:-
1. That after great persuasion both the parties agreed to live separately and for this the petitioner (Aryan Raj @ Rajnikant Kumar) offered to pay Rs.
15,00,000/- (Rupees Fifteen Lakhs Only) as full and final settlement amount to the Patna High Court CR.
MISC. No.49286 of 2025(3) dt.03-11-2025 Opposite Party No. 2 (Amrita Swaraj).
Opposite Party No. 2 accepted the offer and gave her consent.

2. That the husband/petitioner agreed to pay the aforesaid settlement amount in the sum of Rs.
15,00,000/-
(Rupees Fifteen Lakhs Only) in seven equal instalments in following manner:-
(A) The petitioner (Aryan Raj @ Rajnikant Kumar) shall pay first installment of Rs.
2,15,000/- (Rupees Two Lakhs fifteen Thousand) on the date of furnishing bail bond in the concerned Court.
The payment shall be made through Bank Draft in the name of opposite party No. 2 (Amrita Swaraj) and remaining six installments will be paid before 10th of each succeeding month.
3. That four wheeler vehicle (Swift Desire) bearing No. JH15AA3928 will be transferred as vehicle is in the possession of in the name of Aryan Raj @ Rajnikant Kumar, since 16.02.2021.
all the remaining installments will be paid by the Opposite Party No. 2 or concerned who was paying.

4. That both the parties have agreed to file the mutual divorce petition in terms of Section 13(B) of the Hindu Marriage Act, before the Principal Judge, Family Court, Patna after disposal of the Criminal Miscellaneous No. 49286 of 2025.

sentences.text: That both the parties have further agreed to withdraw respective cases Civil/Criminal (i). Patna City Complaint Case No. 769 of 2022, (ii) Matrimonial Case No. 885 of 2022, (iii) Nalanda Complaint Case No. 495 of 2022 and (iv) Patna High Court CR.

entities.text: Patna City Complaint Case No. 769 of 2022
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: dt.03-11-2025 Matrimonial Case No. 139 of 2022 and if any cases in nature filed against each other in the light of settlement of dispute soon after filing of the mutual divorce petition.
6. This settlement shall be full and final settlement and no party shall claim in future against each other, in any manner.

7. That both the parties agreed to file mutual consent divorce case under Section 13(B) of Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, before Principal Judge, Family Court, Patna as mentioned above and after that both the parties are free to lead their life as per their own will.
8. That the above contents of the agreement have been read over and explained to us in Hindi which are have fully understood and accepted there upon.

9. That in the above terms and conditions the present settlement has been arrived at between the parties and both parties have signed in presence of their learned counsels, who have also put their signature on this agreement.
5. Learned A.P.P. for the State has vehemently opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail of the petitioner.

6. Considering the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case, let the above named petitioner, in the event of his arrest/surrender within a period of six weeks from today, be enlarged on anticipatory bail on furnishing bail-bond of Rs.
20,000/- (Rupees twenty thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the learned court concerned, Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.49286 of 2025(3) dt.03-11-2025 Patna City, Patna in connection with Complaint Case No. 769(c)/2022 subject to conditions as laid down under section 482(2) of the B.N.S.S.
7.

If so advised, either of the parties will be at liberty to make an application before the Court below for referring the matter to the District Mediation Centre for the purpose of reconcilation or one time settlement.
8. The application stands allowed.

(Chandra Prakash Singh, J) amitkr/-
